decisions.quote:
After
confirming the initial findings in standard search, we tested the same manipulation in multiple-target search, Thornton and
Gilden’s (2007) hybrid standard/multiple-target search, and simple- and selective enumeration. The RT slope differences between
real- and illusory contours did not replicate in Thornton and Gilden’s task, though they did in multiple-target search and selective
enumeration.
decisions.reason: The shipped coding truncated a sentence in the abstract to code the replication as failed based solely on Experiment 3 (Thornton and Gilden's hybrid task). Across the paper's experiments testing Li, Cave, and Wolfe (2008), Experiment 1 (standard visual search, closely replicating Li et al.'s Experiment 3) confirmed the original RT slope findings, and Experiments 2 (multiple-target search) and 5 (selective enumeration) also replicated the RT slope differences between illusory contours and real-contour controls, whereas Experiment 3 did not replicate the RT slope differences. Under the codebook rules, when a close replication and several conceptual replication tasks confirm the original finding alongside a task that explicitly does not replicate it, the aggregated outcome is mixed.
